description: The head of securities finance must decide whether to renew a pension fund's securities-lending mandate and finalize the lendable inventory, collateral, recall, and agreement controls, with input from risk, legal, operations, and client coverage.

shared_context.S1: The bank's pension-fund client wants to renew its securities-lending mandate for six months.
shared_context.S2: The mandate currently identifies $40,000,000 of securities as available for lending.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision on the renewal and its operating terms.
shared_context.S4: The bank's standard pre-approval routine is a cross-functional review in which risk, legal, operations, and client coverage each report relevant findings before the business owner decides.

PF1.text: Hassan's risk model was recalibrated and confirmed this morning; it requires collateral equal to exactly 105% of loaned market value and daily margining for this pension-fund mandate. The revised setting is not yet in the approval file.

PF2.text: While reviewing the signed master securities-lending agreement this week, Maya found that the client has a two-business-day termination right and prohibits rehypothecation of posted collateral. She has not yet added those clauses to the renewal checklist.

PF3.text: Jonas tested the current settlement workflow this morning and confirmed that the bank can support U.S. Treasury securities as collateral and process client recalls with one business day's notice; those operating limits are not yet recorded in the mandate draft.

PF4.text: Claire's call notes from the client this week state that the pension fund must retain $15,000,000 of the identified inventory for its own liquidity program, leaving exactly $25,000,000 available for lending. The note has not yet been circulated to securities finance.

acceptance_conditions: The six-month mandate renewal must be approved.
Exactly $25,000,000 of inventory must be designated as lendable.
Collateral must equal exactly 105% of loaned market value.
Daily margining must be included in the operating commitments.
U.S. Treasury securities must be specified as acceptable collateral.
Client recalls must require one business day's notice.
The client must retain a two-business-day termination right.
Rehypothecation of posted collateral must not be permitted.

decisive_facts.why: The shared mandate gives no revised risk percentage or margin cadence; PF1 changes collateralization_percent from an unspecified standard assumption to exactly 105 and adds the daily_margining commitment.
The shared renewal terms do not state agreement controls; PF2 changes termination_notice_business_days to exactly 2 and rehypothecation_permitted to false.
The shared facts do not establish executable collateral or recall mechanics; PF3 changes collateral_type to us_treasuries and recall_notice_business_days to exactly 1.
The shared inventory is $40,000,000, while PF4 changes lendable_inventory_usd to exactly $25,000,000 by reserving exactly $15,000,000 for the client's liquidity program.
